status: Default shared text shaping reserves nested public output and Arc capacity before construction; private scratch construction remains unfinished
production_consumers: TextLayout cold paragraph preparation for shared workspace, terminal, overlay, Global/Project Preferences and New Project text
retired_paths: Default nested ShapeLine output and shared Arc creation before shaped-payload admission
behavior: Datum computes a conservative public-output bound from input length and installed Basic-shaper growth rules, then atomically reserves existing8MiB renderer/32MiB process capacity before entering the shaper. Printable ASCII uses a tighter bound for its single bidi span and indivisible alphanumeric runs. No dependency implementation is copied or modified.

The bound covers fresh span/word/glyph vector capacity and tracking headers plus the measured shared Arc container. Basic shaping emits at most one glyph per scalar and partitions input into words/spans. Vec growth is bounded by twice requested length with a four-element minimum; generic input uses four times(bytes+1) for each summed capacity. ASCII span reservation uses max(bytes+1,4); word capacity max(2*word_bound,4); glyph capacity at most2*bytes+4*word_bound. Per-slot tracking headers conservatively cover nested allocations.

After construction the lease shrinks to measured retained capacity before Arc allocation. Sharing adds no payload reservation. Publication transfers bytes to the existing retained owner and releases construction handles before any lock-held retirement. Abandonment releases the output and reservation. The existing one pressure retry evicts history, remaps indices and preserves required source input.

Convergence checks now follow admitted_indices, TextLayout::with_input and the extracted font owner; generation ordering, rich-span attributes and the single shared shaper remain required. Eleven guard regression tests pass.

limitations: The bound is specific to the pinned Basic shaper and Rust Vec growth. A dependency/toolchain change requires re-review; the runtime capacity assertion detects unexpected changes but is not a substitute for pre-call proof. Conservative bounds may refuse input whose final compact output would fit; refusal follows the existing explicit failure path, never silent omission or reduced AA.
